literal: Kaitai year 8 restored it with Han households.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 8 it was re-established for Han settlers.

literal: There are Buluo Spring, Jinhe Mountain, Yehu Ridge, and Baidao Slope.
idiomatic: It has Buluo Spring, Jinhe Mountain, Yehu Ridge, and Baidao Slope.

literal: One county:
idiomatic: One county:

literal: Xuande County.
idiomatic: Xuande County.

literal: Originally Han Tongguo County land, belonging to Yunzhong Commandery; later subordinate to Dingxiang Commandery; abolished at the end of Han.
idiomatic: It was Han Tongguo County in Yunzhong Commandery, later in Dingxiang Commandery, abandoned in late Han.

literal: Northern Qi set Zi'a Fort.
idiomatic: Northern Qi established Zi'a Fort.

literal: Tang Huichang era established the county.
idiomatic: Tang's Huichang period created the county.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Zhenwu County.
idiomatic: Zhenwu County.

literal: Originally Han Dingxiang Commandery Shengle County.
idiomatic: It was Han Dingxiang Commandery's Shengle County.

literal: Backed by the Yin Mountains, fronting the Yellow River.
idiomatic: It lay against the Yin Mountains with the Yellow River before it.

literal: Northern Wei once made Shengle its capital—this was the place.
idiomatic: Northern Wei once held its capital at Shengle—here.

literal: Tang Wude year 4 conquered the Turks and built the Yunzhong area command.
idiomatic: Tang Wude year 4, after defeating the Turks, established the Yunzhong area command.

literal: Linde year 3 changed it to the Chanyu grand area command.
idiomatic: Linde year 3 it became the Chanyu grand area command.

literal: Shengli year 1 again changed it to the Anbei area command.
idiomatic: Shengli year 1 it was renamed the Anbei area command.

literal: Kaiyuan year 7 cut off and subordinated to Eastern Shouxiang Fort.
idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 7 it was detached and placed under Eastern Shouxiang Fort.

literal: Year 8 established the Zhenwu Army military commissioner.
idiomatic: Year 8 created the Zhenwu Army command.

literal: Huichang year 5 it became the Anbei grand protectorate.
idiomatic: In Huichang year 5 the seat was raised to the Anbei grand protectorate.

literal: Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong appointed his elder brother Siben Zhenwu military commissioner.
idiomatic: Later Tang Zhuangzong made his elder brother Siben military commissioner of Zhenwu.

literal: Taizu year 1 of divine enthronement, returning from campaigning against the Tuyuhun, attacked it and took all its people east; only three hundred local militia remained to garrison.
idiomatic: In the Taizu's first year of divine enthronement, returning from a Tuyuhun campaign, he attacked the place, deported the entire population eastward, and left only three hundred local militia on guard.

literal: Later it was again made a county.
idiomatic: Later it was restored as a county.

literal: Yunnei Prefecture, Kaiyuan Army, lower grade, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Yunnei Prefecture—Kaiyuan Army, lower grade, with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally Middle Shouxiang Fort land.
idiomatic: It was originally Middle Shouxiang Fort.

literal: At the founding of Liao the Dai-north Yun-Shuo pacification office was set up; changed to Yunnei Prefecture.
idiomatic: Early Liao placed the Dai-north Yun-Shuo pacification office here, later renamed Yunnei Prefecture.

literal: Early Qingning it was promoted.
idiomatic: It was raised in rank at the start of Qingning.

literal: There are Weisai Army, ancient Khotan city, Datong River valley, Tian'an Army, Yongji Palisade, Anle garrison, and Fuyun Mound.
idiomatic: It has Weisai Army, ancient Khotan city, the Datong River valley, Tian'an Army, Yongji Palisade, Anle garrison, and Fuyun Mound.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Southwest Pacification Office.
idiomatic: Its military affairs came under the Southwest Pacification Office.

literal: It governed two counties: Rourou County.
idiomatic: It administered two counties: Rourou County.

literal: Ningren County.
idiomatic: Ningren County.

literal: Tiande Army—originally Middle Shouxiang Fort.
idiomatic: Tiande Army was originally Middle Shouxiang Fort.

literal: Tang Kaiyuan abolished Hengsai Army and placed Tian'an Army in the Datong River valley.
idiomatic: Under Tang Kaiyuan Hengsai Army was abolished and Tian'an Army established in the Datong River valley.

literal: Qianyuan era changed it to Tiande Army and moved to Yongji Palisade; the present seat is this.
idiomatic: In the Qianyuan period it became Tiande Army and shifted to Yongji Palisade—the present headquarters.

literal: The Taizu pacified the Tangut and then broke Tiande, carrying off all officials and people east.
idiomatic: After pacifying the Tangut the Taizu stormed Tiande and deported every official and commoner eastward.

literal: Later a pacification office was placed; gradually it became a settled town, and a member of the imperial clan was made Tiande Army military commissioner.
idiomatic: A pacification office followed; as settlement grew a clansman was appointed Tiande Army military commissioner.

literal: There are the Yellow River, Heishan Pass, Lucheng, Weisai Army, Qin Great Wall, and Tang Great Wall;
idiomatic: It has the Yellow River, Heishan Pass, Lucheng, Weisai Army, the Qin Great Wall, and the Tang Great Wall;

literal: There is also Mount Mona; Qian'erzui Fort lies to its north.
idiomatic: Mount Mona stands here; Qian'erzui Fort lies north of it.

literal: Ningbian Prefecture, Zhenxi Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Ningbian Prefecture—Zhenxi Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Tang Long Fort; Liao established it.
idiomatic: It was Tang's Long Fort; Liao founded the prefecture.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Southwest Pacification Office.
idiomatic: Its military affairs came under the Southwest Pacification Office.

literal: Fengsheng Prefecture, Wuding Army, upper grade, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Fengsheng Prefecture—Wuding Army, upper grade, with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally Tang Xin Prefecture.
idiomatic: It was originally Tang Xin Prefecture.

literal: Later Tang set a training commissioner commanding the eight mountain-rear armies; Zhuangzong appointed his brother Cunju.
idiomatic: Later Tang placed a training commissioner over the eight mountain-rear armies; Zhuangzong gave the post to his brother Cunju.

literal: The army mutinied, killed Cunju at Qizhou, and the great generals led Lu Wenjin to flee and submit.
idiomatic: Troops mutinied, slew Cunju at Qizhou, and great generals escorted Lu Wenjin in flight to surrender.

literal: The Taizu took Xin Prefecture; Zhuangzong sent Li Siyuan to recover it.
idiomatic: The Taizu seized Xin Prefecture; Zhuangzong dispatched Li Siyuan to retake it.

literal: Tongguang year 2 raised Weisai Army.
idiomatic: Tongguang year 2 promoted it to Weisai Army.

literal: Later Jin Gaozu ceded it in tribute; Emperor Taizong raised its rank.
idiomatic: Later Jin Gaozu ceded the region; Liao Emperor Taizong elevated it.

literal: There are Lianghe Confluence, hot springs, Longmen Mountain, and Zhuolu Mountain.
idiomatic: It has the Lianghe Confluence, hot springs, Longmen Mountain, and Zhuolu Mountain.

literal: Three hundred li southeast to Nanjing; four hundred forty li northwest to Western Capital.
idiomatic: It lay three hundred li southeast of Nanjing and four hundred forty li northwest of Western Capital.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Western Capital metropolitan deployment office.
idiomatic: Its military affairs came under the Western Capital metropolitan deployment office.

literal: It governed three prefectures and four counties: Yongxing County.
idiomatic: It administered three sub-prefectures and four counties: Yongxing County.

literal: Originally Han Zhuolu County land.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Zhuolu County.

literal: The Yellow Emperor fought Chiyou here.
idiomatic: Here the Yellow Emperor battled Chiyou.

literal: Eight thousand households.
idiomatic: Eight thousand registered households.

literal: Fanshan County.
idiomatic: Fanshan County.

literal: Originally Han Jundu County.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Jundu County.

literal: The mountain yields white-green alum, hence the name.
idiomatic: White-green alum comes from the mountain, giving the county its name.

literal: There are Fanshan and the Sanggan River.
idiomatic: It has Fanshan and the Sanggan River.

literal: Sixty li south of the prefecture.
idiomatic: It stood sixty li south of the prefecture.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Longmen County.
idiomatic: Longmen County.

literal: There is Longmen Mountain—cliff faces cliff, several hundred feet high, looking from afar like a gate.
idiomatic: Longmen Mountain rises here: opposing cliffs hundreds of feet high that from a distance resemble a gate.

literal: Peripheral rivers and desert floodwaters all pass here toward the sea.
idiomatic: Outlying rivers and desert runoff all converge here on their way to the sea.

literal: When it rains water in a moment exceeds ten ren; when clear it is shallow enough to ford—a truly vital choke point controlling the northern frontier.
idiomatic: Rain can raise the water ten ren in moments; in fair weather it is shallow enough to wade—a critical northern frontier pass.

literal: Two hundred eighty li northeast of the prefecture; four thousand households.
idiomatic: It lay two hundred eighty li northeast of the prefecture with four thousand households.

literal: Wangyun County.
idiomatic: Wangyun County.

literal: Originally Wangyun River valley land.
idiomatic: It was originally the Wangyun River valley.

literal: Emperor Jingzong built a hidden residence here; thus a market town formed.
idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong established a concealed residence here, and a market town grew up around it.

literal: When Emperor Muzong died, Jingzong entered to succeed the Guozhong lineage, styled Yuzhuang.
idiomatic: After Emperor Muzong's death Jingzong entered to inherit the Guozhong line, taking the style Yuzhuang.

literal: Later Wangyun County was established, directly subordinate to Zhangmin Palace and attached here as a dependency.
idiomatic: Later Wangyun County was created, reporting directly to Zhangmin Palace as a dependency of this prefecture.

literal: Two hundred sixty li northeast of the prefecture.
idiomatic: It stood two hundred sixty li northeast of the prefecture.

literal: One thousand households.
idiomatic: One thousand registered households.

literal: Guihua Prefecture, Xiongwu Army, upper grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Guihua Prefecture—Xiongwu Army, upper grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Xialuo County.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Xialuo County.

literal: Northern Wei changed it to Wende County.
idiomatic: Northern Wei renamed it Wende County.

literal: Tang raised it to Wu Prefecture; Emperor Xizong changed it to Yi Prefecture.
idiomatic: Tang promoted it to Wu Prefecture; Emperor Xizong renamed it Yi Prefecture.

literal: Later Tang Taizu restored Wu Prefecture; Emperor Mingzong again made it Yi Prefecture; Emperor Lu restored Wu Prefecture.
idiomatic: Later Tang's Taizu restored Wu Prefecture; Mingzong made it Yi again; Emperor Lu returned it to Wu Prefecture.

literal: Later Jin Gaozu ceded it to Liao; the present name was adopted.
idiomatic: Later Jin Gaozu ceded it to Liao and the present name was given.

literal: There is the Sanggan River;
idiomatic: It has the Sanggan River;

literal: Huihe River valley;
idiomatic: the Huihe River valley;

literal: Aiyang River valley;
idiomatic: the Aiyang River valley;

literal: Mount Tanshan, also called the pass head.
idiomatic: Mount Tanshan, also known as the pass head.

literal: There is a Cool Hall where Empress Chengtian took the cool; thirty li northeast of the mountain is New Cool Hall where Emperor Jingzong took the cool—only pine arbors over several passes.
idiomatic: A Cool Hall stands where Empress Chengtian summered; thirty li northeast is New Cool Hall where Emperor Jingzong summered—nothing but pine shelters over several passes.

literal: Duanyun Ridge—extremely high and steep, hence the name.
idiomatic: Duanyun Ridge is sheer and lofty, giving it its name.

literal: Four hundred fifty li northwest to Western Capital; it governed one county: Wende County.
idiomatic: It stood four hundred fifty li northwest of Western Capital and governed one county: Wende County.

literal: Originally Han Nuqi County land.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Nuqi County.

literal: Northern Wei established it; ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Northern Wei founded it with ten thousand households.

literal: Kehan Prefecture, Qingping Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Kehan Prefecture—Qingping Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Pan County; abolished under Northern Wei.
idiomatic: It was Han Pan County, abolished under Northern Wei.

literal: Northern Qi set Northern Yan Commandery and changed it to Huairou County.
idiomatic: Northern Qi created Northern Yan Commandery and renamed it Huairou County.

literal: Sui abolished the commandery; it belonged to Zhuo Commandery.
idiomatic: Sui abolished the commandery and placed it in Zhuo Commandery.

literal: Tang Wude era restored Northern Yan Prefecture; the county remained as before.
idiomatic: Tang's Wude period restored Northern Yan Prefecture; the county kept its old name.

literal: Zhenguan year 8 changed it to Gui Prefecture.
idiomatic: Zhenguan year 8 it became Gui Prefecture.

literal: In the Five Dynasties the Xi king Quzhu moved several thousand tents to Gui Prefecture and set himself apart as Western Xi, styled Kehan Prefecture;
idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties Xi king Quzhu migrated several thousand households to Gui Prefecture, split off as Western Xi, and styled the seat Kehan Prefecture;

literal: The Taizu followed this arrangement.
idiomatic: The Taizu adopted the arrangement.

literal: There is Gui Spring in the city; tradition says Shun married his two daughters here.
idiomatic: Gui Spring flows within the walls; tradition holds that Shun wed his two daughters here.

literal: There are also hot springs, Ban Spring, Mojishan Mountain, Jiming Mountain, Qiao Mountain, and Li Mountain.
idiomatic: It also has hot springs, Ban Spring, Mojishan Mountain, Jiming Mountain, Qiao Mountain, and Li Mountain.

literal: It governed one county: Huailai County.
idiomatic: The prefecture administered a single county, Huailai.

literal: Originally Huairou County; the Taizu changed the name.
idiomatic: It was Huairou County until the Taizu renamed it.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Ru Prefecture, Jinyang Army, middle grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Ru Prefecture—Jinyang Army, middle grade, with a prefect.
